Research

Building human-scale vascular systems

Our work combines stem cell technology, biomaterials, and microfluidics across three connected research directions.

01 / MATERIALS

Engineering human ECM biomaterials

Animal-derived matrices are common in tissue engineering, but differences between species can change how human cells behave. We aim to develop human ECM-like hydrogels using iPSC-derived cells, creating a more relevant foundation for engineered vessels.

Human cells · Hydrogels · Matrix biology
02 / VESSELS

Engineering functional microcirculation

We build vessel models with the cells and supporting structures needed for long-term function, then connect arterioles, capillaries, and venules in a single network. The goal is to study flow, exchange, and vascular disease in systems that resemble human microcirculation.

Microfluidics · 3D templates · Flow
03 / TISSUE

Vascularized skin grafts

Engineered skin often lacks functional microvessels, limiting how quickly it integrates after grafting. We are working to incorporate perfusable vessels into skin constructs to support survival and repair.

Engineered skin · Perfusion · Regeneration
